title: There's a new way to break RSA that's faster than anything we've seen before
gist: Researchers led by UC San Diego's Nadia Heninger devised a classical signature-forgery attack on textbook (blind-signature) RSA that avoids factoring, cutting security to roughly 2^65, 2^90 and 2^119 operations for 1024-, 2048- and 4096-bit keys, below the 2^128 standards threshold. Padded PKCS/PSS RSA is unaffected, but blind-signature systems like Privacy Pass (used by Apple and Cloudflare) are exposed, adding urgency to migrating off RSA.

insights.claim: A new signature-forgery method breaks RSA keys without factoring, overturning the long-held assumption that RSA is as hard to break as factoring large integers.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Undermines a core assumption behind decades of RSA risk models; expect cryptographic migration timelines to be revisited.
insights.quote: RSA is as difficult to break as it is to factor large integers, at least so we thought. The researcher suggests that you can practically break RSA without cracking its key.

insights.claim: Forging a 1024-bit signature took about 1,380 CPU core-years versus an estimated 500,000 to 1 million core-years to factor the key, a reduction of orders of magnitude.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Brings 1024-bit key forgery within reach of well-funded actors much sooner than previously estimated.

insights.claim: The researchers coded the attack by hand without AI or GPUs, and Heninger said such tools will almost certainly lower the security levels further.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Current estimates are a ceiling, not a floor; expect follow-on work to cut costs further.

insights.claim: The attack uses a variant of the 'special' number field sieve, invented in 2007, run against an oracle that returns yes-or-no answers to queries, which PKCS and PSS padding eliminate.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Mechanism explains exactly which deployments are exposed: those without padding.

insights.claim: The attack only works against blind-signature (textbook) RSA; the overwhelming majority of RSA in use relies on PKCS or PSS padding and is safe.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Mainstream TLS and signing infrastructure is not at immediate risk; avoid overreacting to headline risk.

insights.claim: Privacy Pass, an anonymous-authentication protocol used by Apple and Cloudflare among others, is the best-known real-world system relying on textbook RSA and thus exposed to the forgery attack.

insights.claim: Attacking Privacy Pass would require compromising a server of Cloudflare, Apple or another operator and generating 2^43 signatures, roughly the volume of network traffic Cloudflare says it handles in about a day, though regular key rotation greatly reduces the odds of success.
